title: Fynaptix · AI & Compute Research
heading: AI & Compute Intelligence
subheading: The capex supercycle, silicon stack, foundation-model giants & the bubble debate
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. AI is the market's most crowded trade; concentration and drawdown risk are significant. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Amazon (~$220B), Alphabet ($195–205B), Microsoft (~$190B CY2026 / ~$255–260B FY2027 all-in), Meta ($130–145B) and Oracle (S&P models $90–95B FY2027) — combined $825–855B, unchanged: no hyperscaler has reported since the last edition. Goldman Sachs estimates the five AI hyperscalers will spend ~$1.2T next year. The test is this week and next: Meta reports Wed Oct 21 after the close (confirmed), Microsoft and Alphabet on Oct 28 (same week as the Oct 27–28 FOMC), Amazon in late October. The binding constraint this week was financing, not demand: the 10-year yield sat ~5.05–5.25% (24-year highs) and the Broadcom CEO said financing could be a bigger obstacle to AI expansion than chips or power. Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle had issued more than $228B of bonds by Oct 13 (CNBC), which is why funding costs matter so much

At a private investor meeting on Oct 14, Anthropic reportedly disclosed Q3 revenue of $16.8B (FT) — ~+50% QoQ versus ~+140–145% in Q2 — and said it was cash-flow positive and adjusted-profitable, with an 85% GAAP gross margin per a Bloomberg reporter. Markets had hoped for faster growth (Jefferies: expected run-rate of at least $80B vs. ~$67B annualized Q3) and the data point fed the chip selloff; IPO valuation talk has drifted from $2T+ toward ~$1.5T–$2T (~30x annualized Q3 revenue at $2T) and the registration statement was still pending as of Oct 16 after two delays. OpenAI's annualized revenue was ~$50B at end-September (FT, not the ~$70B reported earlier — a gross-vs-net accounting gap); Bloomberg says it still expects ~$70B+ by year-end. Its $30B+ round at ~$1.4T is in talks with no lead investor chosen, and the IPO is now 2027 or later

kpis.sub: SOXX 8-DAY LOSING STREAK; AI/CHIP MARKET CAP LOST
kpis.label: The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) fell eight straight sessions through Oct 15 — about −12.7% cumulatively and the longest losing streak in its 11-year history (Dow Jones Market Data) — and the top-20 global AI/semiconductor stocks lost over $1 trillion (CNBC). Triggers: a hot September CPI (raising bets on more Fed hikes), Treasury yields above 5%, the Anthropic growth deceleration, CoreWeave's debt (~$46–50B net debt, bonds yielding near 15%), Intel and Broadcom CEO financing warnings, and China memory-chip competition (CXMT). Nasdaq closed −1.88% on Oct 15 at 26,693 and fell again Oct 16 (~26,140 per one tally), S&P 500 ~7,659, roughly 1% below its record; SK Hynix fell 10%+ and Samsung ~9% in Asia. SOXX is −8% for October but still up 60%+ in 2026. By Oct 16 CoreWeave had slipped another ~7% (shares ~−15% on the week), its bonds briefly yielded above 16% and 5-year CDS topped 1,000bp (Roic/Reuters); Fed Chair Warsh said the AI spending surge is adding to inflation

Nvidia closed near $214 on Oct 15–16 (data sources conflict slightly), about 12% below its Oct 6 intraday record of $243.37, after sliding with the chip complex despite no company-specific bad news; CEO Jensen Huang said Nvidia did not need to endorse CoreWeave, sparking a neocloud rebound (CRWV +5.9% on Oct 15 after −16% the day before). Q2 FY27 revenue was $96.2B (+106%, Data Center $89.0B) at ~75% gross margin; Q3 guide ~$108B ±2% (~+89%, a slowing rate of growth); $150B buyback increase leaves ~$235B through FY2028. Bulls (Dan Ives) call the selloff 'a financing issue, not a demand issue'; bears point to Nvidia underwriting its customers (OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, CoreWeave) while buying back stock. Q3 FY27 results are expected in November. Separately, IDC data show Nvidia's China AI-accelerator share fell to 34% in H1 2026 (shipments −44% YoY) as Huawei rose to 28%

tiers.label: Compute & Silicon — the Checks Get Cashed Here
tiers.note: Tiered by role in the stack — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Closed near $214 on Oct 15–16 (−12% from the $243.37 record of Oct 6) in the eight-day chip selloff, with no company-specific bad news. Record Q2 FY27 revenue $96.2B (+106%), Data Center $89.0B, ~75% gross margin; Q3 guide ~$108B ±2% (~+89%). $150B buyback increase leaves ~$235B through FY2028; reported capacity commitments include up to $84.5B from Anthropic and xAI through 2029, and Nvidia is reportedly in talks to anchor up to $10B of Anthropic's IPO. Huang declined to 'endorse' CoreWeave on Oct 15
rows.watch for: Customer funding is the live risk: Anthropic's Q3 growth slowed to ~+50% QoQ, OpenAI's run-rate reset to ~$50B, and CoreWeave's bonds yield near 15% — all Nvidia customers or channel partners. Circular-financing optics (BIS: 55.2% of AI-firm investment comes from other AI firms) persist. TSMC's 'no sign of a slowdown' commentary is the offsetting demand signal; Nvidia reports in November. China is a second pressure point: IDC puts Nvidia's H1 2026 China share at 34% versus Huawei's 28%

rows.angle: Supplies Anthropic ~3.5GW of Google TPU capacity from 2027 and designs future TPUs through 2031; Anthropic's leaked S-1 lists ~$161B of Broadcom equipment-lease contracts, and the WSJ reports Broadcom is arranging $50B+ of financing for custom chips developed with OpenAI. Fiscal Q3 AI semiconductor revenue was $16.7B (+221% YoY) with a ~$115B FY2027 / ~$230B FY2028 outlook (Sept 2). On Oct 12 CEO Hock Tan warned financing could be a bigger obstacle to AI expansion than chip or power shortages, and the stock fell with the group in the eight-day selloff
rows.watch for: Tan's own warning is the point: Broadcom's growth is underwritten by two cash-burning labs (OpenAI, Anthropic) and vendor-style financing, and Anthropic's growth deceleration plus higher rates raise the cost of that financing. Custom silicon is a win for Broadcom but the clearest sign Nvidia's customers are building alternatives

rows.angle: Fell with the group in the Oct 15 selloff (−1.5%) after the SOXX's record eight-day streak; the 6GW OpenAI GPU agreement (with a warrant for up to 160M AMD shares) ties a large part of the AI story to OpenAI's ability to keep funding compute. Consensus target ~$565 (Stifel $635, Piper Sandler $600); Q2 Data Center revenue +107% to $6.7B. Reports Q3 on Nov 3
rows.watch for: The OpenAI revenue reset and higher financing costs sit squarely on the OpenAI-dependent portion of AMD's story; ROCm-versus-CUDA remains unresolved. Nov 3 earnings is the next hard data point

rows.angle: Q3 (reported Oct 15): revenue $46.7B (+41% YoY, above the $44.6–45.8B guide), net income NT$763B (+69%, a record), gross margin 66.4% (2nm ramp), operating margin 58.7%. Q4 guide $52.3–54.3B revenue, 65–67% gross margin — reportedly >$4B above Street expectations; the 2026 outlook now implies ~43–45% growth (guided 'slightly above 40%' in July), $60–64B 2026 capex. CEO C.C. Wei saw 'no sign of a slowdown'. Yet the stock fell ~9% for the week (−1.8% on Oct 15) with the chip complex. Holds an estimated ~72% of global foundry revenue
rows.watch for: A record quarter and raised outlook did not stop the selloff — evidence the market is pricing financing and rates, not demand. 2027 commentary and customer concentration ('Customer A', reportedly Nvidia, was 19% of 2025 revenue) matter next; Taiwan geopolitical risk remains the sector's biggest tail risk. ASML (Oct 14) reported Q3 profit of €4.96B vs. ~€4.1B expected, lifted its 2026 sales floor to €44–45B and said customers are asking for 2029–2030 tools

Reports Wed Oct 21 after the close (confirmed)

Largest OpenAI-dependent backlog of the group (RPO $664B in fiscal Q1 FY27; net debt ~$132B), revenue +30% and Cloud Infrastructure +121%, but FY26 free cash flow was −$23.7B with capex outrunning operating cash flow. private_watchlist.name: Anthropic
private_watchlist.value: ~$1.5–2T IPO TALK · Q3 REVENUE $16.8B (+50% QOQ) · REGISTRATION PENDING
private_watchlist.note: At an Oct 14 private investor meeting Anthropic reportedly disclosed Q3 revenue of $16.8B (FT) — growth of ~50% QoQ versus ~140% in Q2 — plus positive cash flow, adjusted profitability and an 85% GAAP gross margin (per a Bloomberg reporter). Markets had wanted faster growth; IPO valuation chatter has drifted from $2T+ toward ~$1.5T–$2T (~30x annualized Q3 at $2T). The leaked S-1 (Sept 29) showed 2025 revenue ~$4.6B, a $42B 2025 net loss and $518B of compute commitments ~80% non-cancellable; reports have said a roadshow the week of Nov 9 and up to $100B raised, but the registration statement was still pending as of Oct 16 after two delays. All figures are press reports and subject to change. Last confirmed private mark is $965B (Series H, May 28); on Oct 16 some current and prospective investors were reportedly weighing a lower IPO valuation.

private_watchlist.name: OpenAI
private_watchlist.note: Annualized revenue was ~$50B at end-September per the FT (the ~$70B figure included gross cloud-partner sales); Bloomberg says it expects ~$70B+ by year-end, with Q3 run-rate growth reported at ~77% (unaudited). The $30B+ round at ~$1.4T (~64% above March's $852B mark) is in talks — MGX and other UAE funds up to $10B, BlackRock in talks, no lead chosen. Reported 2026–2030 cash burn is ~$278B. Altman has ruled out a 2026 IPO; this round is expected to be the last before listing. Broadcom is reportedly arranging $50B+ of financing for OpenAI's custom chips (WSJ).

private_watchlist.name: Mistral
private_watchlist.note: Closed a €3B (~$3.49B) Series D on Sept 8 — the largest-ever equity round by a European tech company — led by Samsung Electronics and co-led by EQT's Scaleup Europe Fund and PSG Equity, at a post-money valuation above €21B (~$24.4B), nearly double its prior mark. Nvidia, ASML and BlackRock were among the participants, alongside new investors including Luxembourg's sovereign fund. (Unchanged this edition.)

private_watchlist.name: Waymo
private_watchlist.value: $126B VAL · MAKING ITS SAFETY CASE AHEAD OF TESLA CYBERCAB
private_watchlist.note: Published its argument in early September that fully autonomous driving needs multiple sensor types and that "pure end-to-end" AI isn't yet safe enough — timed just ahead of Tesla's Sept 3 Cybercab launch. Continues running 14 cities, 4,000+ vehicles, ~500K paid rides/week and ~4M autonomous miles/week, including the new Harry Reid Airport authorization. NHTSA probes into the Santa Monica child collision and Austin school-bus incidents remain open. (Unchanged this edition.)

bear_case.title: The revenue gap
bear_case.description: The industry has committed an estimated $3–4T to AI infrastructure against an annualized return requirement of roughly $600–800B in new profit, while AI-attributable revenue runs an estimated $50–150B a year. OpenAI's ~$50B run-rate (not ~$70B) and Anthropic's slowdown to ~+50% QoQ growth ($16.8B Q3) show the two largest buyers of compute are growing slower than the market modeled; Goldman now sees ~$1.2T of hyperscaler spend next year. Counterpoint: Anthropic is reportedly cash-flow positive at an 85% GAAP gross margin, TSMC guided Q4 more than $4B above Street, and ASML says customers want 2029–2030 tools — Dan Ives argues the selloff is 'a financing issue, not a demand issue.' The BIS still names an AI-capex bust among its top three risks.

bear_case.title: AI's own architects sound the alarm
bear_case.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published "We Must Pace the Frontier" on Sept 12, arguing AI capability growth has accelerated "drastically faster" since summer 2026 — driven mainly by AI's growing ability to build the next generation of AI — and proposing independent safety evaluation, inter-lab coordination and international cooperation. OpenAI's Sam Altman and DeepMind's Demis Hassabis publicly backed the call; days later Palantir's Alex Karp went further, telling CNBC that frontier labs may need to be nationalized over "unlimited risk." The market reaction was real — chip names sold off while Meta, Alphabet and Microsoft rose — but skeptics note that a company mid-prep for a ~$2T IPO calling for the industry to slow down is also a moat-building and regulatory-capture argument, not purely an act of altruism.

bear_case.title: Rates and financing are now the transmission mechanism
bear_case.description: A hot September CPI (Oct 14) raised bets on further Fed hikes (one tally: ~69% odds of a December hike; FOMC Oct 27–28), with the 10-year at ~5.05–5.25% and the 30-year ~5.6% near 24-year highs. SOXX fell eight straight sessions (−12.7%, longest streak in its history) and >$1T of AI/chip market value was lost. CoreWeave (~$46–50B net debt, ~8x trailing EBITDA) saw bonds yield near 15% and shares drop 16% on Oct 14; Broadcom's Hock Tan and Intel's CEO warned financing may be the real constraint. Counterpoint: the S&P 500 sits only ~1% from its record, defensives rotated up, TSMC and ASML posted record results, and Nvidia's CEO says he is 'optimistic'. Update Oct 16: CoreWeave bonds briefly yielded >16% with 5-year CDS above 1,000bp, though a credit analyst stressed it is not an imminent-default signal; Fed hike odds for October were only ~17% (CME) with December still debated, and IG's Axel Rudolph framed the rout as about construction financing rather than collapsing demand.

bear_case.title: Off-balance-sheet obligations turning concrete
bear_case.description: Moody's flags ~$662B of signed-but-not-commenced data-center lease commitments off hyperscaler balance sheets, and the RBA's Oct 1 Financial Stability Review put hyperscaler obligations via SPVs and vendor financing at US$1–1.5T, financed with 20–30 year debt against hardware of 'uncertain economic lives'. Anthropic's leaked S-1 adds a lab-level data point: $518B of compute commitments, ~80% non-cancellable or take-or-pay. The RBA also noted aggregate leverage remains contained. Oracle remains the starkest case (BBB-, FY26 FCF −$23.7B, S&P ~$42B FY27 deficit) and fell 5.5% on Oct 8 and 4.6% on Oct 15; Oracle's RPO is $664B against net debt of ~$132B.

bear_case.title: Circular financing
bear_case.description: The BIS (Bulletin 137, Oct 1) found 55.2% of investment value into 1,246 AI-supply-chain firms came from other AI firms, 28.7% of AI firms' invested value went to other AI firms, and 46.4% of AI-to-AI deal value involved supply-chain relationships. New this week: Broadcom is reportedly arranging $50B+ of financing for OpenAI's custom chips, Anthropic's S-1 shows ~$161B of Broadcom equipment-lease contracts, and Nvidia is in talks to anchor up to $10B of Anthropic's IPO. Burry calls Nvidia's revenue 'majority circularly financed'. Counterpoint: the BIS frames this as a feature of a young supply chain rather than proof of systemic risk, and Anthropic's reported path to adjusted operating profit suggests at least one lab can fund itself. This week's wrinkle: Nvidia's CEO said it did not need to endorse CoreWeave, a neocloud Nvidia has backed, as CoreWeave's debt spooked credit markets.

bear_case.title: Depreciation clock
bear_case.description: Hyperscalers depreciate AI hardware over 5–6 years; Burry argues replacement cycles are really 2–3 years, understating depreciation by ~$176B across 2026–2028 and inflating Oracle's earnings by ~27% and Meta's by ~21%. On Sept 27 Nvidia published data arguing A100/H100/B200 hardware retains value beyond accelerated depreciation schedules, and on Oct 2 Burry replied by citing the 1960s computer-leasing bubble ('The Money Game'). Bull evidence: CoreWeave's CEO says H100 capacity was rebooked at ~95% of the original contract price and Nvidia says A100s are rented through 2029 — nine years after launch. Bear evidence: that is rental pricing for the best-contracted capacity, not proof the economic life of the whole installed base is 5–6 years. CoreWeave, whose business model rests on GPU residual values, is the live stress test as its debt costs spike.

bear_case.title: Layoffs while capex soars
bear_case.description: Layoffs.fyi's tracker showed 128,536 tech workers cut across 299 companies in 2026 through Sept 10 (not refreshed this edition) — already exceeding all of 2025 — while a broader tracker (SkillSyncer, different methodology) counts 210,741 workers across 383 layoff events through Sept 20. xAI itself cut roughly 500 data-annotation staff (a third of that team) on Sept 12 as part of a stated pivot to "specialist AI tutors." The juxtaposition — record infrastructure spend, record layoffs, and AI labs restructuring their own workforces — keeps fueling the argument that AI economics lean partly on cost-cutting elsewhere, not purely on AI revenue.

bear_case.title: Concentration everywhere
bear_case.description: AI is simultaneously the market's largest index weight, VC's largest allocation (OpenAI and Anthropic alone took over 40% of a record $510B global H1 2026 venture total, and AI took 86% of all US venture dollars in H1 per PitchBook), and this hub's connective thread — a drawdown would hit robotics, nuclear, storage and quantum sentiment at once. NVIDIA now sits at the center of deals spanning chips (TSMC, Broadcom), model hosting (Hugging Face), enterprise software (Palantir) and a potential anchor stake in Anthropic's IPO — a single company's balance sheet increasingly touches nearly every layer of this page, even as customers like Anthropic simultaneously build Google TPU alternatives. Counterpoint: infrastructure vendors keep posting record quarters and Oracle's Sept 10 beat is a live example — some strategists call the bear case premature given actual demand signals. Crunchbase puts Q3 2026 global venture at $159B (−25% vs Q2), with AI taking 64% ($102B) and a record 27 billion-dollar rounds (Databricks and SSI $5B each; Crusoe, Moonshot AI and Mistral $3B+) — fewer, bigger bets.

catalysts.title: Broadcom and Intel CEOs warn on AI financing

catalysts.title: Hot CPI, CoreWeave debt scare and Anthropic's Q3 numbers

ASML the same day beat on profit (€4.96B) and lifted its 2026 sales floor to €44–45B.

catalysts.title: Software joins the selloff

CoreWeave fell another ~7% with bond yields above 16%; reports said some Anthropic IPO investors were weighing a lower valuation.

positions.note: Clearest capex-payback story (~$220B capex, AWS +37%) and a core Anthropic supplier, whose Q3 was reportedly cash-flow positive at $16.8B revenue; the slowdown to +50% QoQ is the thing to watch in late-October earnings.

positions.name: TSMC
positions.note: Least circularly-financed name here: record Q3 (revenue $46.7B, +41%; profit +69%), Q4 guide >$4B above Street and 'no sign of a slowdown' — yet the stock fell ~9% in the week, which is a rates story, not a demand one.

positions.name: NVIDIA
positions.note: Best fundamentals on the page (China share down to 34% per IDC) (Q3 guide ~$108B, ~75% margin) but ~12% off its $243 record at ~$214 as its customers' funding (OpenAI ~$50B run-rate, CoreWeave bonds near 15%) comes under scrutiny. Also sits in the Quantum, Robotics and AI Biotech sleeves — don't double-count.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.note: Diversified cash flows cushion its OpenAI exposure (~$190B CY2026 capex, ~$80B Azure backlog), but the Oct 28 print will show how OpenAI-linked backlog holds up after the ~$50B run-rate reset. Also in the Quantum sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: Broadcom
positions.note: Moved down from Core: CEO Hock Tan himself warned on Oct 12 that financing may constrain AI expansion, and growth now rests on two cash-burning labs (~$161B of Anthropic lease contracts, $50B+ of financing for OpenAI chips) as Anthropic's growth slowed to +50% QoQ.

positions.name: AMD
positions.note: Fell 1.5% in the Oct 15 selloff; priced near the ~$565 consensus target and tied to OpenAI's 6GW GPU deal, which the ~$50B revenue reset and higher funding costs put in question — Nov 3 earnings is the next test.

positions.name: Oracle
positions.note: Fell 4.6% on Oct 15 after 5.5% on Oct 8: RPO of $664B against ~$132B net debt, FY26 FCF −$23.7B and a BBB- rating make it the weakest balance sheet to own with long yields above 5%.

positions.name: CoreWeave
positions.note: Bonds yield near 15% with ~$46–50B of net debt (~8x trailing EBITDA) and the stock fell ~16% on Oct 14 and ~7% more on Oct 16 (CDS >1,000bp) — the cleanest read on AI credit stress, and a name whose business rests on GPU residual values.

positions.name: Palantir
positions.note: Fell ~5% to ~$190 on Oct 16 into a correction as software sold off on financing worries (IGV −4%); excellent growth (~82% guided) but still a very high multiple with little cushion if AI sentiment turns.

positions.name: Meta
positions.note: Reports this week with a ~$1.9T cap and a $130–145B capex guide; the Muse launch lifted shares but funding costs raise the bar for returns, and the org whiplash keeps capex discipline an open question.

positions.name: UiPath
positions.note: ~13% growth versus triple-digit AI-native peers, and software sold off again on Oct 16; numbers, not narrative, must show agents are a tailwind to RPA.

positions.name: SpaceX
positions.note: AI thesis rests on Nvidia dependence and xAI capex of $15.8B in Q2; the frontier-challenger economics are unproven and the spectrum deal is a separate business.
